lead.headline: SpaceX Wins $55bn AI Chip Plant — IPO Hits $1.8tn Valuation
lead.they_say: AI capex is peaking. Broadcom's $300bn+ market cap wipeout on a revenue miss proves the AI trade is overheating. The semiconductor cycle is turning down.
lead.reality: SpaceX secured tax exemption for a $55bn AI chip manufacturing plant, Google upsized equity raising to $85bn for AI spending, and Meta is rolling out AI agents on WhatsApp for monetization. Three separate infrastructure bets at billion-dollar scale, all active simultaneously. The Broadcom miss is a company-specific ASIC-to-GPU rotation, not a sector demand collapse.
lead.thesis: The AI compute buildout is accelerating through the Broadcom noise. The $300bn wipeout creates the buyable dip in NVDA and AMD. The signal is capital allocation — follow where the money goes, not where headlines point.
lead.actors: SpaceX, Elon Musk, Google/Alphabet, Meta, Broadcom, NVIDIA, AMD
lead.invalidation_trigger: NVDA closes below $145 on >2x volume, or SpaceX delays IPO filing past Q3 2026
paradigm_implications: AI compute concentration shifts semiconductor supply chains from Taiwan-dependent to US-based fabrication
SpaceX IPO at $1.8tn would be largest in US history — resets valuation benchmarks for the entire AI ecosystem
lead.capital_flow_implication: Capital rotates from Broadcom/ASIC plays into GPU-fabrication plays (NVDA, AMD) and AI infrastructure ETFs (AIQ, BOTZ). Follow the $85bn Google raise and $55bn SpaceX plant.
lead.portfolio_implication: Portfolio implication: buy NVDA on Broadcom spillover dip with 5% invalidation stop; accumulate satellite/defense ETFs (ITA, PPA) ahead of SpaceX IPO; trim Broadcom exposure until custom-chip demand signals stabilize.

stories.headline: Trump's Iran War Drains US Oil Stocks to Lowest Level Since 2004
stories.they_say: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire and Republican House pushback signal de-escalation. The oil risk premium should contract.
stories.reality: US crude inventories hit two-decade lows. Gulf states are actively negotiating pipeline routes to bypass the Strait of Hormuz — a contingency you only plan if you expect the strait to close. Ceasefire headlines don't refill storage tanks.
paradigm_implications: Energy corridor fragility is a structural repricing, not a headline-driven blip
Hormuz bypass pipelines would reshape global oil trade routes permanently
stories.portfolio_implication: Portfolio implication: buy CL on dips to $72 with invalidation at $68; accumulate energy infrastructure ETFs (XLE, OIH) on structural supply thesis rather than headline chase.

stories.headline: Broadcom Loses $300bn as Revenue Forecast Disappoints
stories.they_say: The AI trade is over. Broadcom's -$300bn is the canary in the semiconductor coal mine — capex cuts are coming.
stories.reality: Broadcom's revenue miss is a company-specific rotation from custom ASIC chips to GPU clusters. Google ($85bn), SpaceX ($55bn), and Meta (WhatsApp AI) are increasing, not decreasing, AI infrastructure spend. The $300bn wipeout is a rotation signal, not a sector peak.
paradigm_implications: Semiconductor leadership is rotating from custom-chip plays to GPU/fab plays
Company-specific corrections in a secular growth trend = buying opportunities
stories.portfolio_implication: Portfolio implication: sell Broadcom into strength, rotate proceeds into NVDA and AMD for the GPU infrastructure buildout; use defined-risk put spreads for protection on further contagion.

stories.headline: Bessent Calls US Inflation Jump a 'Short-Term Blip' as Services CPI Holds at 4.1%
stories.they_say: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the latest inflation spike is transitory and driven by one-off energy effects from the Iran conflict.
stories.reality: Services inflation is running at 4.1% — largely independent of energy prices. The Fed's Beige Book shows steady employment and higher inflation. A 'blip' that's been persistent for 18+ months is a trend, not a blip.
paradigm_implications: The Fed's tightening bias stays alive regardless of oil price swings
Sticky services inflation means rate cuts are further away than bond markets price
stories.portfolio_implication: Portfolio implication: trim duration in fixed income; prefer TIPS and floating-rate notes over nominal treasuries; add gold on pullbacks to $2,350 as real rate hedge.

stories.headline: Hurricane Trump Threatens to Blow China Off Course
stories.they_say: China's industrial policy is executing at 5-year-plan tempo — insulated from US political cycles and tariff noise.
stories.reality: Trump's Iran war + tariff escalation create the first major external stress test for Beijing's export-driven growth model. A leading Chinese property developer reports massive losses. Japan's defence minister publicly rebuffs Chinese 'new militarism' claims. The 'hurricane' metaphor is apt — China is being blown off its planned course.
paradigm_implications: China's industrial policy faces its first real external stress test since Belt and Road
Capital may rotate from China-exposed EM equities to India/SE Asia alternatives
stories.portfolio_implication: Portfolio implication: underweight China-exposed EM ETFs (EEM) relative to India (INDA) and ASEAN (EEMA); add short-duration CNH bonds for carry, not growth exposure.

stories.headline: Suspected Sabotage of Deep-Sea Cable Triggers First NATO-Led Response
stories.they_say: Undersea cable damage is a routine maritime incident — repair ships will handle it. No strategic implications.
stories.reality: NATO activated its first-ever collective response to suspected cable sabotage — a threshold has been crossed. Hybrid warfare against critical infrastructure now triggers the Alliance's Article 5-adjacent mechanisms. This is a new doctrine in action.
paradigm_implications: Critical infrastructure protection becomes a NATO-core mission, expanding defense budgets beyond troop commitments
Maritime infrastructure insurance premiums reprice globally — second-order inflation input
stories.portfolio_implication: Portfolio implication: add cybersecurity ETFs (HACK, CIBR) and defense contractors (RTX, LMT) on NATO infrastructure protection mandate; marine insurance plays (CB, MKL) beneficiaries of premium repricing.
